applicability_notes: All behavioral claims about curl flags are version-pinned to curl 8.10.1 via tag-exact manual sources. Current-manual passages were used as locators and cross-checked; where the current manual differs (transient set adds 522/524; --retry-max-time decimal seconds added 8.16.0), the 8.10.1 text governs and the deliverable follows it. Introduction-version table proves availability in 8.10.1, not semantics; semantics come from the manual texts.

claim_map.inference: max_attempts=4 maps to --retry 3 (1 initial + 3 retries). Draft --retry 4 allows 5 attempts. Mapping arithmetic is inference from the source statement.
claim_map.source_statement: If a transient error is returned when curl tries to perform a transfer, it retries this number of times before giving up. Setting the number to 0 makes curl do no retries (which is the default).

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: Current online manual adds HTTP 522/524 to this list (post-8.10.1 change); those codes are NOT transient in 8.10.1 and the deliverable excludes them.
claim_map.inference: 404 and most 4xx are never retried by --retry alone (also stated in retry-all-errors.md).
claim_map.source_statement: Transient error means either: a timeout, an FTP 4xx response code or an HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504 response code.

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: --retry-delay disables the algorithm; server Retry-After overrides per-attempt delay.
claim_map.source_statement: When curl is about to retry a transfer, it first waits one second and then for all forthcoming retries it doubles the waiting time until it reaches 10 minutes which then remains delay between the rest of the retries.

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: Applies when the response carries a Retry-After header.
claim_map.inference: Critique 6 (support arrived after 8.10.1) is factually false: 7.66.0 predates 8.10.1 and the sentence is present verbatim in the 8.10.1 source.
claim_map.source_statement: curl complies with the Retry-After: response header if one was present to know when to issue the next retry (added in 7.66.0).

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: Documented for any error class; duplicate-data risk is the stated reason to avoid default use and redirected I/O.
claim_map.inference: Extending this to mutating POST endpoints risks duplicate mutations; rejected under retry_scope=read_only_get. Risk direction (duplicates) is source-stated; the product-scope refusal is constraint reasoning.
claim_map.source_statement: Retry on any error. This option is used together with --retry. This option is the sledgehammer of retrying. Do not use this option by default (for example in your curlrc), there may be unintended consequences such as sending or receiving duplicate data.

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: With --retry, some transient HTTP codes retry; most 4xx still do not. With --fail, HTTP error codes fail/retry.
claim_map.inference: The draft claim that all unsuccessful HTTP statuses already produce curl errors is false without a failure option.
claim_map.source_statement: By default curl does not return error for transfers with an HTTP response code that indicates an HTTP error, if the transfer was successful. For example, if a server replies 404 Not Found and the reply is fully received then that is not an error. / By default, curl does not consider HTTP response codes to indicate failure.

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: Mutually exclusive with --fail. Not fail-safe for 401/407 during authentication (fail.md).
claim_map.inference: Chosen for the launcher so HTTP 400+ yields error 22 while the body is preserved for the failed-run diagnostic.
claim_map.source_statement: Return an error on server errors where the HTTP response code is 400 or greater. This option allows curl to output and save that content but also to return error 22.

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: Decimal values allowed (added 7.32.0); integer 45 used so no version concern.
claim_map.inference: Because the counter resets per retry, --max-time 45 cannot bound total wall-clock time across attempts.
claim_map.source_statement: Set maximum time in seconds that you allow each transfer to take. If you enable retrying the transfer (--retry) then the maximum time counter is reset each time the transfer is retried.

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: Timer includes inter-retry sleeps; checked before each new retry; zero disables retry timeout. Decimal-seconds acceptance (current manual, added 8.16.0) postdates 8.10.1 and is not used.
claim_map.inference: Because an in-progress attempt may overrun the limit, --retry-max-time 45 plus --max-time 45 still cannot guarantee a 45s absolute bound; a supervisor deadline is required.
claim_map.source_statement: The retry timer is reset before the first transfer attempt. Retries are done as usual (see --retry) as long as the timer has not reached this given limit. Notice that if the timer has not reached the limit, the request is made and while performing, it may take longer than this given time period.

claim_map.applicability: Availability of all cited options in curl 8.10.1
claim_map.conditions_exceptions: Introduction proves availability, not that later semantic changes were present; semantics verified against the 8.10.1 tag-exact texts above.
claim_map.inference: All cited options predate 8.10.1, so no cited feature is anachronistic.

claim_map.conditions_exceptions: No source statement either way; curl manual silence is not evidence for or against a product feature.
claim_map.inference: Critique 3 rejected by constraint reasoning: cancellation is original obligation O5 and evidence does not authorize deleting original product constraints. No curl source cited for this disposition.
